feature: AI Integration — Finding Enrichment & Auto-Remediation Loop
mvp: Phases 1-4 (enrichment + full auto-remediation loop). Phase 5 (plugins) deferred.
core_principles: wolf owns findings — wolf scans are the sole source of findings; the AI never creates, discovers, or adds findings. AI only fixes findings or proves their validity (false-positive triage).
AI is optional — wolf must remain fully functional with no AI configured; deterministic path is the guaranteed baseline.
out_of_scope: Egress allowlisting for the AI runner container
existing_infrastructure: findings carry Fingerprint, Category, Status (incl false_positive), enrichment fields
Loops UI exists but hidden; backend engine intact

phases.name: Surfaces
phases.verification: go build ./... && go test ./internal/... && cd ui-next && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build

user_stories.title: Deterministic enrichment template engine
user_stories.description: As a security engineer, I want each finding turned into a structured fix prompt assembled from data wolf already has, with no AI call.
acceptance_criteria: Builds ai_fix_prompt with fixed sections: Problem, Location+snippet, Repo context, Task, Acceptance criteria
Repo context includes function/module, file purpose, dependents, CWE, rule remediation when present
Deterministic — same finding in, same prompt out
Unit test: full-field finding produces all sections; missing fields omitted gracefully
go build ./... and go test ./... pass

user_stories.title: enrich command with filter expression
user_stories.description: As a user, I want wolf enrich to write fix prompts into a scan's findings JSON for the findings I select.
acceptance_criteria: wolf enrich --scan <id> populates ai_fix_prompt in the findings JSON artifact
Filters --severity, --category, --tool, --exclude-path (glob), --ids work and combine (AND)
Findings outside the filter untouched
Re-running enrich is idempotent
Test: --severity critical,high touches only those rows
go build ./... and go test ./... pass

user_stories.title: Optional AI-generated guidance layer
user_stories.description: As a user with an AI provider configured, I want enrich --ai to produce model-authored remediation guidance.
acceptance_criteria: enrich --ai calls the provider per selected finding, stores guidance in ai_fix_prompt
With no provider, --ai fails clearly; deterministic template path unaffected
AI calls recorded in ai_logs
Test: noop provider degrades --ai to the template
go build ./... and go test ./... pass

user_stories.title: Hybrid AI tool registry
user_stories.description: As an operator, I want to add a CLI AI agent by config without recompiling; raw-API engines stay in Go.
acceptance_criteria: CLI tool definitions (name, command, arg template, cwd, success rule) read from settings store
Unknown/misconfigured tool yields a clear error, no panic
Existing ClaudeCode/Codex/Custom engines still resolve
Raw OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic API engines selectable
Test: a config-defined CLI tool is discoverable via the registry
go build ./... and go test ./... pass

user_stories.title: AI runner container
user_stories.description: As the loop, I need a writable, networked container with git and AI CLIs so an agent can edit the repo.
acceptance_criteria: Runner image ships git + supported AI CLIs
Loop launches it with repo bind-mounted read-write, network enabled, API keys injected from secrets store
Container removed after the loop ends
Verification: a loop invocation writes a file in the mount, visible on the host path
go build ./... passes

user_stories.title: Raw-API patch mode
user_stories.description: As a user pointing the loop at a plain LLM endpoint, I want wolf to obtain and apply a patch itself.
acceptance_criteria: wolf prompts for a unified diff and applies it via git apply
On rejection, re-prompts with the apply error, retries up to the per-finding fix budget
Budget exhausted -> batch marked failed; loop continues
Test: a malformed patch triggers a retry then a failed-batch outcome
go build ./... and go test ./... pass

user_stories.title: Loop iteration — triage, plan, fix, rescan
user_stories.description: As a user, I want one loop iteration to triage findings, make the AI plan and fix, then rescan with wolf to validate.
acceptance_criteria: Iteration: AI triage -> plan artifact written -> agentic fix or raw-API patch -> wolf rescan
Agentic tool receives the whole targeted findings set + meta-prompt
Fingerprint comparison across the wolf rescan classifies findings fixed/still-present/new; AI claims not trusted
Agentic tool commits preserved; uncommitted remainder committed by wolf on wolf/fix-<scanid>
Test: a stubbed AI engine editing a file yields a committed iteration and a rescan delta
go build ./... and go test ./... pass

user_stories.title: Loop stop conditions
user_stories.description: As a user, I want the loop to end correctly — success, exhaustion, or guardrail.
acceptance_criteria: Stops when targeted findings reach 0 (success)
Stops when a configured severity threshold is met
Stops when an iteration reduces targeted findings by 0 (no progress)
Stops (and may revert) on regression — verify command non-zero exit or increased finding count
Verify command auto-detects from language; repo verify_command overrides
Per-finding fix budget exhaustion marks a finding ai_unfixable
Test: each stop condition independently exercised with a stub
go build ./... and go test ./... pass

user_stories.title: AI triage of false positives
user_stories.description: As a user, I want the AI's false-positive calls applied but reviewable — proving a finding invalid, never deleting it.
acceptance_criteria: AI-triaged false positive gets status false_positive, the AI reason, triaged_by=ai; finding row retained
Excluded from loop success counting
Listed for human review at loop end
Test: a triaged finding does not block a reached-0 success exit
go build ./... and go test ./... pass

user_stories.title: Determinism manifest & AI I/O capture
user_stories.description: As an auditor, I want every loop run fully reconstructable from records.
acceptance_criteria: Each iteration writes a manifest: git SHA before/after, scanner image digests, tool set, fingerprints in/out, AI tool, plan reference
Scanner image digests pinned across the loop
ai_logs extended with loop_id, iteration; prompt/model/params/raw response/applied patch persisted
Iteration 2+ meta-prompts include a prior-iteration summary
Test: a two-iteration loop produces two manifests and linked logs
go build ./... and go test ./... pass

user_stories.title: Cost & time ceilings
user_stories.description: As an operator, I want optional spend/time caps.
acceptance_criteria: --max-iterations mandatory and enforced
Optional per-invocation timeout kills a hung batch, marks it failed
Optional total token/$ budget stops the loop when crossed
Optional overall wall-clock cap stops the loop when crossed
Loop stops at whichever ceiling triggers first; manifest records the stop reason
Test: a tiny $ budget stops a loop early with the correct reason
go build ./... and go test ./... pass

user_stories.title: wolf loop CLI + loop REST API
user_stories.description: As a user, I want to start and watch a loop from the CLI and API.
acceptance_criteria: wolf loop --scan <id> [--max-iterations N] [--ai-tool X] [--min-severity S] [budget/timeout flags] runs and streams progress
POST /api/loops starts a loop; GET /api/loops/{id}/stream streams events; GET /api/loops/{id} returns status
A loop against a non-git repo fails fast with an actionable error
Test: API + CLI both start a loop and receive iteration events
go build ./... and go test ./... pass

user_stories.title: Revive & update the Loops UI
user_stories.description: As a user, I want to configure, run, and watch a loop in the browser.
acceptance_criteria: Loops nav entry, route, and command-palette item un-hidden
Start-loop form: pick scan, AI tool, max iterations, severity target, optional ceilings
Live view shows per-iteration progress, plan artifact, per-iteration diff, manifest, cost meter
TypeScript typecheck and build pass
Verify in browser: start a loop, watch iterations advance

user_stories.title: Container-plugin system for paid scanners (deferred)
user_stories.description: As an operator, I want to add a paid SAST/DAST scanner by config — still wolf-owned findings.
acceptance_criteria: A plugin is a config entry: name, image, invocation, secret refs, output format (SARIF or wolf JSON)
Existing container runner executes it; output normalized into the findings table
Secrets injected from the encrypted secrets store
Missing/invalid plugin config yields a clear error
Test: a stub plugin emitting fixed SARIF produces normalized findings
go build ./... and go test ./... pass

definition_of_done: All acceptance criteria in US-1..US-13 pass
Phases 1-4 verified by their verification commands
go vet ./internal/... and cd ui-next && npx tsc --noEmit pass
go build ./... and cd ui-next && npm run build succeed
With no AI configured, all non-AI behavior unchanged (NFR-1)
No AI code path creates a finding row (FR-0)
A loop run produces a PR-ready wolf/fix-<scanid> branch, per-iteration manifests, plan artifacts, ai_logs entries
Loops UI verified in a browser
